newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - June 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - June 17.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.

- A unified financial watchdog board will be established under the direct control of the prime minister, with a commission under its control which will replace the current three separate regulatory bodies in banking, securities and insurance.

- The government is seeking ways to render substantial assistance to an alleged former Korean comfort woman for Japanese imperial forces who now lives in Cambodia, in Addition to arranging her first visit in 54 years to her hometown near Pusan.

- President Kim Young-sam will visit the United Nations and Mexico June 23 through 28, he will attend the U.N.-sponsored global environmental summit meeting in New York and will make a state visit to Mexico.

- Pusan Mayor Moon Jung-soo denied having accepted money from Chung Tai-soo, chairman of the failed Hanbo Group, in the first session of the trial of chairman Chung and eight politicians in one of the country's biggest bribery scandals.
